stories.summary: Define the system:scheduler and system:worker principals and their policy grants
stories.description: ADR 0009 section 6: distinct, narrowly scoped system principals that are audited like a human and can never approve a plan. Inert in this story: nothing binds them yet.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-10-28 on master cd09a83, STACKED on the enterprise-enforcement-closeout stand-in (this plan is blocked_by ENF-03) - a stand-in of every story in decision-routing and system-principals applied together with it. First run 2 conflicts in this plan: tests/unit/test_scheduler_daemon.py::test_run_daemon_wires_advance_all_plans_as_reconcile_fn (`reconcile_fn is advance_all_plans`) and tests/unit/test_scheduler_daemon_scan_watchdog.py::test_scheduler_daemon_imports_remain_stdlib_or_pipeline (the daemon may import only stdlib and pipeline) - both re-scoped in SYS-02 (bind inside the watchdog worker; import through pipeline.actor). Re-run: 17746 passed / 21 skipped, 0 conflicts from this plan. Four other failures are environment-only and fail identically on untouched master in the planning container (test_aider_harness_availability x2: proxy-injected GH_TOKEN; test_docs_have_no_personal_home_path: the container HOME is the root user's home, which the guard bans by value; test_remote_sync ssh: no ssh binary).

TARGET IMPLEMENTER: cloud open-source (Claude-class sizing, every mechanically checkable requirement graded below). Provider/model are NOT pinned: dispatch resolves them from the live model registry's `roles.dispatch` entry.

WHY: the scheduler daemon and dispatched workers act as the unbound `LOCAL_OPERATOR` (pipeline/actor.py), so the audit stream cannot tell a human's merge from the scheduler's, and a compromised worker inherits every right the operator has.

WHAT TO BUILD:
1. app/identity.py: `SYSTEM_SCHEDULER = Principal(subject="system:scheduler", auth_method="system")` and `SYSTEM_WORKER = Principal(subject="system:worker", auth_method="system")`; a subject starting `system:` is reserved: `OidcProvider`'s mapping must never yield one (add the check where the issuer-qualified subject is built in app/oidc.py, or assert it cannot happen because subjects are `<issuer>#<sub>`, and test that).
2. app/policy.py `LocalPolicy`: an explicit grant table. `system:scheduler` -> the actions the daemon tick performs. Static analysis on cd09a83 (with the enforcement-closeout gates) found exactly these reachable from `advance_all_plans` and `scan_all_plans`: `plan:dispatch` (pipeline/dispatch.py dispatch_story; advance_pipeline, review_story and mark_story_in_progress after ENF), `story:merge` (pipeline/merge.py), `story:mark_done` (pipeline/ci.py), `story:interrupt` (pipeline/advance.py's interrupt_story calls). `plan:pause` (only the pause/resume tools) and `story:patch` (worker-side tools) were NOT found reachable: do not grant them. Re-run the same grep (`authorize(` / `refusal_for_host_config(` call sites) before you start and list each grant with its call site in the commit body; if the code has moved, the grep wins over this list. `system:worker` -> `story:patch` only (checkpoint, status, request_decision on its own story; story scoping is a later story). Both are denied `plan:approve`, `plan:reject`, `plan:ingest`, `config:write`, `decision:answer` unconditionally - including when a manifest names them as owner or delegate (ownership must not apply to `system:` subjects; ADR 0009 forbids a scheduler approving its own work).

DOCS: docs/specs/IDENTITY_AND_POLICY.md section 4 "System principals" row and section 6 step 3 (defined; binding is SYS-02).

TESTS (new tests/unit/test_system_principals.py): each granted action allowed for the scheduler; every forbidden action denied; a manifest naming `system:scheduler` as owner, and one naming it as a delegate, still deny it `plan:approve` and `plan:reject`; worker allowed story:patch, denied plan:dispatch and story:merge; an OIDC token whose sub is `system:scheduler` does not yield the system principal.

GENERAL RULES (every step of this story):
- Write the failing tests first (CLAUDE.md Step 3) and confirm they fail on an assertion, not an import error.
- Verify with the full suite `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` AND `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check .` AND `.venv/bin/python scripts/check_line_limit.py`; all must be green before you finish. Report pass/fail counts in the PR description.
- A new test file that imports any `pipeline.*` module must `import pipeline.server` first (pre-existing import cycle). Copy the idiom in tests/unit/test_triage_cap_silent_skip.py.
- Bind a non-operator principal in tests the way tests/unit/test_patch_plan_enforcement.py does (`pipeline.actor.bind_principal`); never add an `actor` parameter to any MCP tool (a guard test forbids it).
- The harness scratchpad `.agent_scratchpad.md` stays untracked. Commit only the files this brief names plus the new test files it asks for. Add no helper scripts, dumps or module copies.
- Never modify an existing test except as this brief pre-authorizes, with the literal edit given. If another pre-existing test fails because of a change this brief requires, do NOT undo the required change - stop and report the conflict, naming the test and the requirement it contradicts.
- Comments and docs you write must stay true after later stories merge: state the invariant, never "until story X lands".
- Cumulative artifacts (the REFERENCE.md policy table, the IDENTITY_AND_POLICY.md section 4 rows, `REMOTE_*` sets): assert only what YOU add or remove (membership/absence), never the full contents, an exact count, or a hash.
- Error messages and logs name the action and the principal subject only - never a token, secret, payload, path or exception text (Secure-by-Design).
- Commit message: Conventional Commits (`<type>(<scope>): <subject>`, subject <=72 chars), body explains why; put the story key in the body. If you change an existing test as pre-authorized, the body must say which test and why (CLAUDE.md Step 4).

stories.summary: Run the scheduler daemon's tick as system:scheduler
stories.description: Bind SYSTEM_SCHEDULER around the daemon's reconcile and watcher calls so the audit stream attributes scheduler actions to the scheduler.

This is a gate that can WITHHOLD WORK: if the grant set misses one action the tick performs, that action is silently denied every tick and the pipeline stops (.claude/rules/testing-config-gates.md). A green mocked suite does not prove the grant set.

SCOPE IS DECIDED, NOT A FINDING (preflight): do NOT wrap `reconcile_fn`/`scan_fn` in `run_daemon` - tests/unit/test_scheduler_daemon.py::test_run_daemon_wires_advance_all_plans_as_reconcile_fn asserts `reconcile_fn is advance_all_plans`. And pipeline/scheduler_daemon.py may import only stdlib and `pipeline` (tests/unit/test_scheduler_daemon_scan_watchdog.py::test_scheduler_daemon_imports_remain_stdlib_or_pipeline), so it must not import `app.identity`.

WHAT TO BUILD:
1. pipeline/actor.py: re-export `SYSTEM_SCHEDULER` (it already imports `app.identity`); mark the import `# noqa: F401 (re-exported)`.
2. pipeline/scheduler_daemon.py (988 lines - change at most 4 lines): both phases (scan and reconcile) run through `_run_with_watchdog`, which calls `fn()` inside the nested `_worker` on a new `threading.Thread`. A ContextVar bound in the main thread does NOT reach that thread, so bind there: inside `_worker`, wrap `box["result"] = fn()` in `with bind_principal(SYSTEM_SCHEDULER):`, importing both names from `.actor` (relative import). That single point covers the startup reconcile, every tick's scan and every reconcile.

REAL-ENVIRONMENT CHECK (required before you finish; paste the output in the PR description): run one full daemon cycle against a scratch plan in a real tmp git repo with enforcement on (a tests/integration test using the real daemon loop with one iteration is acceptable) and print the count of `authorization_denied` records and `denied` audit outcomes. It must be 0, and the audit stream must show `system:scheduler` as the principal of the dispatch.

DOCS: docs/specs/IDENTITY_AND_POLICY.md section 4 "System principals" row (the scheduler is bound; the worker is not yet - see the roadmap's open design question) and REFERENCE.md policy section (one sentence: scheduler actions are attributed to system:scheduler; `PIPELINE_POLICY_ENFORCE` remains the kill switch).

TESTS (new tests/unit/test_scheduler_principal_binding.py): a reconcile_fn and a scan_fn passed to a real `SchedulerDaemon` each observe `current_principal() is SYSTEM_SCHEDULER` inside the worker thread; the main thread's principal is unchanged afterwards; a raising fn still propagates its error; `run_daemon` still passes `advance_all_plans` itself as reconcile_fn (the existing test stays green unmodified).
